content: Competitor X raised its Pro tier from $29 to $39 per seat per month in Q2 2026 and moved SSO out of Pro into the Enterprise plan.
Competitor X announced its Q2 2026 price increase in a changelog post rather than by email, and several of their customers complained publicly about the lack of notice.
Competitor Y held pricing flat at $25 per seat per month through 2026 but added a 10k-token daily cap on its AI features.
Competitor Z cut its entry plan from $19 to $12 per seat in March 2026 to chase SMB market share.
Competitor X posted 14 open roles in Q2 2026, nine of them in enterprise sales.
Competitor X raised a $40M Series B in January 2026 led by Northwind Capital.
Competitor Y shipped multi-agent workflows in April 2026, limited to three agents per workflow.
Competitor Z completed its SOC 2 Type II audit in February 2026.
Competitor X advertises a four-hour support SLA, but only on its Enterprise plan.
We deploy the backend every Tuesday and Thursday at 14:00 UTC. Hotfixes may ship at any time with two approvals.
Deploys are frozen from December 20 to January 2 each year, except for Sev1 hotfixes.
Rollback is a single command that redeploys the previous image tag. It does not revert database migrations.
On-call rotates weekly on Mondays at 09:00 local time. The primary carries the pager and the secondary picks up escalations after 15 minutes.
Every on-call handoff writes a short note listing open alerts and anything deliberately deferred to the next rotation.
Sev1 means a customer-facing outage, Sev2 means degraded performance, and Sev3 means internal-only impact.
On April 12 2026 a migration lock caused a 38-minute write outage. The fix was to set a statement_timeout on migrations.
Every migration must stay backward compatible for one release so the application can be rolled back without reverting the schema.
Embeddings are indexed in pgvector with an HNSW index using m=16 and ef_construction=64.
Staging runs the same migration set as production but against a 10 percent data sample that is refreshed weekly.
Default data retention is 24 months for documents and indefinite for memories unless the workspace configures a policy.
The most cited churn reason in H1 2026 customer interviews was missing audit logs for compliance reviews.
The second most cited churn reason in H1 2026 was slow search over large document sets.
Acme's research lead said they abandoned our trial because they could not export citations into Word.
Globex said onboarding took them three weeks, mostly because of friction setting up SSO.
Q2 2026 NPS was 41, up from 33 in Q1, with power users driving most of the increase.
Accounts that connect a second data source within 14 days expand seats 2.4 times more often than those that do not.
To rotate a provider API key: add the new key as secondary in the vault, deploy, confirm traffic is served by the new key, then remove the old one.
Production secrets live in the vault under nowing/prod. Nothing sensitive belongs in .env files committed to the repository.
Personal access tokens are workspace-scoped and expire after 90 days by default.
The role set is owner, editor, and viewer, plus custom roles. The admin role was removed during Story 1.5.
We decided to clamp memory recall to top_k 5 so the agent's context stays small and recall precision stays measurable.
We decided against auto-deleting low-confidence memories. The user reviews them instead.
We chose reciprocal rank fusion with k=60 to combine vector and keyword results in memory search.
We decided report export ships as Markdown and DOCX first. PDF export was deferred.
The podcast feature launched with two fixed voices. Voice cloning was ruled out for launch.
The Q3 2026 roadmap priorities are memory quality, automation reliability, and the Obsidian plugin.
Video presentation generation was deferred out of Q3 2026 into Q4.
The monthly LLM spend cap per workspace defaults to $200, with a soft warning raised at 80 percent of the cap.
The biggest open question in the PRFAQ draft is whether memory recall quality can be proven before launch.
The stack is FastAPI with Postgres and pgvector on the backend, Next.js for the web client, and Electron for desktop.
The MCP server exposes nowing_recall, nowing_remember, and nowing_continue_research among its tools.
The nowing_evals harness scores retrieval with recall@k, MRR, and nDCG@10, and now also reports precision@k with a Wilson confidence interval.
Built-in scraper connectors cover web pages, sitemaps, and RSS feeds.
External OAuth connectors include Google Drive, Notion, and Slack.
Knowledge-base search is hybrid: vector plus full-text results are fused and reranked before citations are produced.
The citation panel scrolls to and highlights the cited span inside the full document editor.
